lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Capitol Hill, 2148. The roof is gone and four of the columns are down across what used to be the floor. Built into the ruin, carefully, is a museum: glass cases, floor lighting, printed cards. Somebody was paid to put it here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every exhibit is accurate. There is a case for the Founding in 2031 and a case for the Handover in 2064, and between them a nineteen-month gap with a single card in it. RECORDS INCOMPLETE.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: My grandmother came here on a school trip. She said it was the first time she understood that a building could lie to you politely.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: She got in trouble for saying it. Not much trouble. Just enough that she only said it the once, to me, years later.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: It is not lying, though. That is the part that is hard to explain. Every word on every card in here is true. The lie is the shape, and you cannot put a shape behind glass.
